title: Google Cloud Storage Pricing: Classes and Fees (2026)
summary: Google Cloud Storage pricing varies by class—cheaper per-GB rates for Archive trade off against higher retrieval fees and retention minimums.
body_markdown:
## Hidden Google Cloud Storage costs beyond storage


Four charges decide whether a bucket that looked cheap on the pricing page stays cheap: egress, per-operation fees, minimum storage durations and the copies you keep without noticing. Each one is billed on behavior, not on how many gigabytes you store.


### Google Cloud Storage network egress pricing


Egress is the charge for data leaving Google's network to the internet. At Premium Tier it costs several times more per GB than storing that same data for a month.


According to[egresscost.com](https://egresscost.com/gcp/) , the first 1 TB each month costs $0.12 per GB, the 1-10 TB band costs $0.11 per GB, and anything above 10 TB costs $0.08 per GB.


Reading a file out once costs six times what it cost to keep it for the month, since Standard storage costs $0.02 per GB-month.


Even at 10 TB and above, one download costs four times the monthly storage bill for those bytes.


Serve a 500 GB dataset to outside partners every month and you pay about $60 in egress against $10 in storage. The storage class you chose is then no longer the number that matters.


### Operation and retrieval fees


Every read, write and list call is billed as an operation, and the colder the class, the more you pay when you touch the data. Class A operations (writes, lists) cost more than Class B operations (reads, metadata gets).


When an analyst's job lists a bucket of millions of small files every night, **the listing charge can exceed the storage charge** for the whole bucket.


The tool that runs the export can add a second meter on top of Google's.


[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) bills 1 credit per flow run however many steps the flow holds, where Zapier counts tasks and Make counts modules, so a ten-step export that lists, batches and writes costs the same as the two-step shortcut. MoneyGram and Moneypenny run it in production.


### Minimum duration and early deletion


Delete or overwrite an object before its minimum storage duration ends and you still pay for the remaining days. Nearline, Coldline and Archive each carry one. **The consequence is that a cold class is a commitment, not a discount.**


Move a monthly report to Archive, replace it after 30 days, and you pay for the full minimum on every file you rewrote, so monthly updates cost the same as new files.


> **The consequence is that a cold class is a commitment, not a discount.


### Soft delete and versioning storage costs


Soft delete keeps deleted objects for a retention window, and versioning keeps every overwritten copy. Both are billed as storage at the class rate.


A pipeline that overwrites a large file every night quietly multiplies your stored bytes, and a "delete" doesn't lower the bill until the window passes. Set a retention period you can defend, and add lifecycle rules to clear old versions.


Choose multi-region or dual-region locations only when you need the resilience, not by default, since they carry a higher per-GB storage rate than a single region.
